'''Edwin Arend Perkins''' (born 1953)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n85815001.html|title=Perkins, Edwin Arend, 1953-|work=LC Name Authority File|publisher=US Library of Congress|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref> is a Canadian [[mathematician]] specializing in [[probability theory]], including the analysis of [[Brownian motion]] and the applications to probability of [[non-standard analysis]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/edwin-perkins-12084/|title=Professor Edwin Perkins FRS|work=Fellows Directory|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref> He is a [[professor emeritus]] of mathematics and statistics at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ubc.ca/user/2700|title=Ed Perkins|publisher=UBC Department of Mathematics|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Perkins received a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1975 from the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~perkins/cv.html|title=Curriculum vitae|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in 1979 under the supervision of Frank Bardsley Knight at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] with a dissertation titled 'A Nonstandard Approach to Brownian Local Time'.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|4761}}</ref>

He came to the University of British Columbia as a postdoctoral researcher in 1979, and became an assistant professor there in 1982. He was promoted to associate professor in 1985 and full professor in 1989.<ref name=cv/> He was given a tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] in Probability in 2001.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://notes.math.ca/archives/Notesv35n3.pdf|title=Canada Research Chairs in the Mathematical Sciences|page=10|magazine=CMS Notes de la SMC|volume=35|issue=3|date=April 2003|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Perkins was elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (FRSC) in 1988<ref name=crm/> and to the [[Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2007.<ref name=frs/>

He was the 1983 recipient of the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/rollo-davidson-awards-1976-2024|title=Rollo Davidson Awards 1976 – 2024|publisher=University of Cambridge Statistical Laboratory|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref> the 2002 recipient of the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]]<ref name=frs/> and (with [[John McKay (mathematician)|John McKay]]) one of two recipients of the 2003 [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]].<ref name=crm>{{cite web|url=https://www.crmath.ca/en/prizes-and-honours/crm-fields-pims-prize/2003-crm-fields-prize-john-mckay-and-edwin-perkins/|title=The 2003 CRM-Fields Prize awarded to John McKay and Edwin Perkins|work=Prizes and honours|publisher=Centre de Recherches Mathématiques|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref>

In 2019 the University of Illinois gave him their Mathematics Alumni Award for Outstanding Professional Achievement.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://uofi150.news-gazette.com/people/ed-perkins|title=Ed Perkins|department=University of Illinois: 150 Years & Beyond|newspaper=Champaign News-Gazette|access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref>
